articles.title: Maricsa Alfaro: los puntos más controvertidos del fallo que permitió su liberación y las posibilidades de revertir la sentencia
articles.summary: La empresaria fue liberada en los últimos días luego que un tribunal variara su pena de cárcel efectiva por la de prisión suspendida, pese a que atropelló al vigilante Juan Martínez en estado de ebriedad y con el brevete vencido
articles.body_text: Tan solo cuatro meses estuvo en la cárcel la empresaria Maricsa Polet Alfaro Cerna por embestir y causar la muerte al vigilante Juan Martínez Torres, el pasado 3 de mayo, en la urbanización Las Palmas de El Golf, en Trujillo. El pasado 7 de octubre, la Segunda Sala Penal de Apelaciones de La Libertad decidió liberarla. Luego de ser sentenciada -el 5 de junio último- a cuatro años, seis meses y 26 días de prisión, Alfaro Cerna fue recluida en el penal de mujeres El Milagro, pero su defensa presentó una apelación contra dicha condena, por lo que la audiencia se efectuó el 24 de septiembre. El recurso fue analizado por los magistrados Víctor Alberto Martín Burgos Mariños, Jorge Humberto Colmenares Cavero y Manuel Federico Loyola Florián, quienes revocaron el fallo del Tercer Juzgado Penal Unipersonal Transitorio de la Unidad de Flagrancia de La Libertad y determinaron que la denunciada solo cumpla dos años de pena suspendida, es decir, en libertad. Además, establecieron que Alfaro Cerna tiene que comparecer cada 60 días ante el juzgado de ejecución para justificar y registrar sus actividades con el debido control biométrico, no variar su domicilio real sin autorización previa del juzgado de ejecución. Además, está obligada a cumplir con el pago de la reparación civil y no debe cometer un nuevo delito doloso. No obstante, dicho tribunal sí confirmó la decisión de la primera instancia respecto a la inhabilitación definitiva a la empresaria para manejar cualquier tipo de vehículo motorizado. La sentencia de la Segunda Sala Penal de Apelaciones de La Libertad contiene argumentaciones que pueden generar distintas opiniones, en vista que se trata de un caso en el que hay una persona fallecida y la acusada se encontraba en estado de ebriedad, ya que registraba un gramo con ochenta y cuatro centigramos de alcohol por litro de sangre (1.84 G/L), y tenía la licencia de conducir vencida. En su resolución, el tribunal recuerda que el artículo 57° del Código Penal faculta al juez a suspender la ejecución de la pena en caso cumpla ciertos requisitos. Por ello, señala que la pena impuesta a Alfaro Cerna, de 4 cuatro, seis meses y 26 días, “satisface el requisito temporal”. “Resulta inferior al límite legal de la suspensión de la ejecución de la pena”, indicó. Además, aduce que “la acusada carece de antecedentes penales y no registra la condición de reincidente o habitual”. La sala indica que el punto central del debate es el pronóstico sobre la conducta futura de la imputada, es decir que no vuelva a cometer delito doloso. “La defensa sostiene que la acusada colaboró desde el primer momento, se entregó a la policía, cumplió las reglas de conducta, efectuó pagos a cuenta de la reparación civil (que a la fecha suman S/. 130,000.00 soles), aceptó los hechos mediante conclusión anticipada y tiene arraigo domiciliario, familiar y laboral”, indica el tribunal en su argumentación. Incluso, hace hincapié en que el homicidio culposo, delito por el cual fue condenada Maricsa Alfaro, “no es un delito doloso ni se encuentra entre los delitos excluidos de la suspensión por el artículo 57° del Código Penal”. “La gravedad de la conducta ya fue tomada en cuenta al momento de realizar su tipificación (homicidio culposo agravado por conducción en estado de embriaguez); también ha sido valorada al momento imponer la pena de inhabilitación para conducir vehículos motorizados de forma definitiva”, se indica en el fallo. Incluso, remarca que en el expediente del caso no figura evidencia de que la conductora haya intentado fugar. “La acusada no tiene denuncias por incumplimiento de reglas de conducta, entregó su pasaporte, compareció a las diligencias y fue encontrada en su domicilio cuando la autoridad la requirió”, adujo el tribunal. La Segunda Sala Penal de Apelaciones señaló que el delito de omisión de auxilio no fue materia de ejercicio de la acción penal. “Tampoco se ha acreditado denuncia o imputación por omisión de auxilio o fuga del lugar del accidente vinculada a los hechos”, precisa. Además, considera que Maricsa Alfaro “es una persona con actividad laboral conocida y estable (gerente de una empresa), con estudios superiores y sin antecedentes penales” y que los agravantes de manejar en estado de ebriedad y de tener la licencia vencida ya fueron tomados en cuenta en la sentencia y en la inhabilitación para manejar. “La circunstancia de haber conducido con licencia vencida desde el año 2022 y bajo los efectos del alcohol es grave, pero ya fue considerada al momento de determinar el “quantum” de la pena y la inhabilitación (precisamente, la inhabilitación definitiva para conducir cualquier tipo de vehículo motorizados neutraliza el riesgo de reiteración)”, argumentó la sala. Otro hecho saltante de este caso es que se le permitió a la acusada participar en la audiencia de apelación, ya que su defensa planteó que se le interrogue. El magistrado Víctor Burgos Mariños se opuso porque señaló que “no es materia de debate la responsabilidad penal de la procesada, por lo que no cabe interrogarla”. Sin embargo, el tribunal, tras poner a votación el tema, aprobó su participación. El abogado Roberto Arteaga Robles, quien representa a los dos hijos mayores del vigilante Juan Martínez Torres, indicó a El Comercio que, por el lado de la parte demandante, solo puede apelar en el tema de la reparación civil. En el proceso hay otros letrados que ejercen la defensa de los otros cuatro hijos de la víctima. “En el tema de la ejecución no podemos participar porque es un tema del Ministerio Público. Sí podemos argumentar y plantear la nulidad de la sentencia, pero eso queda a discreción de los hijos mayores”, afirmó. Consideró que la Segunda Sala de Apelaciones de La Libertad “ha valorado de forma segmentada” dicho caso. “Una cosa es la apelación de la ejecución, que es por parte de Maricsa Alfaro, y otra cosa es la apelación por la reparación civil. En el tema de la aceptación de la responsabilidad ya no se puede discutir porque ya se aceptó la responsabilidad, solamente se está viendo la ejecución o la suspensión”, afirmó. “No se puede apelar en otro sentido porque en primera instancia fue favorable y ella fue sentenciada. Sí puede apelar el tema de la reparación, pero el tema de la pena no se puede aumentar ni reducir”, agregó. Arteaga explicó que la reciente sentencia estableció que Alfaro Cerna pague una reparación de 400 mil soles, pero la defensa había pedido un monto de 600 mil soles debido a que en el proceso se ha acreditado que Juan Martínez Torres tuvo seis hijos en tres parejas, pero solo se ha reconocido a la esposa. Johnny Aurazo Murrugarra, editor del diario Correo de La Libertad, contó a El Comercio que la liberación de la empresaria Maricsa Alfaro ha causado indignación en la ciudadanía de Trujillo, incluso la prensa local ha tomado con sorpresa esta decisión del Poder Judicial, pues no esperaba un fallo de esta naturaleza. Explicó que los ciudadanos trujillanos cuestionan que en el caso de Adrián Villar, quien atropelló y causó la muerte de la deportista Lizeth Marzano en Lima, se le haya dictado prisión preventiva, mientras que Maricsa Alfaro fue liberada, pese a que se comprobó que manejaba en estado de ebriedad y tenía la licencia de conducir vencida desde el 2022. Incluso, Aurazo Murrugarra aseguró que, de acuerdo con sus fuentes, la noticia de la liberación de Alfaro Cerna también ha sorprendido al Ministerio Público, que esperaba una ratificación de la condena impuesta a la imputada. En cuanto a los integrantes de la Segunda Sala Penal de Apelaciones de La Libertad, Aurazo comentó que se trata de magistrados de “amplia experiencia” y recordó que dos de sus integrantes han estado a cargo de casos de bastante relevancia en el norte del país. En ese contexto, el periodista recordó que los magistrados Víctor Burgos Mariños y Jorge Colmenares Cavero, junto a Manuel Sosaya López, entonces miembros de la Primera Sala Penal de Apelaciones, condenaron en el 2019 a 30 años de cárcel al coronel PNP en situación de retiro y exalcalde de Trujillo, Elidio Espinoza, por el caso ‘Escuadrón de la Muerte’. Además, Víctor Burgos Mariños entabló una querella, en octubre de 2023, a Arturo Fernández, entonces alcalde de Trujillo, debido a que este último lo acusó públicamente de corrupción y de vincularlo con una supuesta red criminal denominada ‘Los Cuellos Blancos del Norte’. La Segunda Sala de Apelaciones de la Corte Superior de Justicia de La Libertad ratificó, en enero del 2026, la condena de un año y ocho meses de pena suspendida para Fernández.

articles.title: La Libertad: realizan pintas con aerosol en muro del complejo arqueológico Chan Chan
articles.summary: Desconocidos realizaron pintas con aerosol negro en un muro perimetral del complejo arqueológico Chan Chan, en Huanchaco, La Libertad. La Dirección Desconcentrada de Cultura deberá evaluar si las inscripciones ocasionaron daños al patrimonio declarado por la Unesco en 1986.
articles.body_text: Desconocidos realizaron pintas con pintura negra en aerosol en uno de los muros perimetrales del complejo arqueológico Chan Chan, ubicado en el distrito de Huanchaco, provincia de Trujillo, en la región La Libertad. Las inscripciones fueron registradas en imágenes difundidas en redes sociales. Hasta el momento, se desconoce cuándo se habría producido el hecho. Las pintas fueron realizadas sobre un muro de adobe de varios metros de altura y más de 600 años de antigüedad, que forma parte de la antigua ciudad capital de la cultura Chimú. Se espera que la Dirección Desconcentrada de Cultura (DDC) de La Libertad emita un pronunciamiento técnico para determinar si las inscripciones ocasionaron daños al patrimonio cultural. En mayo de 2025, la DDC La Libertad denunció la aparición de pintas obscenas en otro espacio del complejo arqueológico. En aquella oportunidad, el equipo de conservadores tuvo que intervenir para retirar los trazos negros del muro afectado. Chan Chan fue reconocido por la Unesco como patrimonio de la humanidad en 1986. Sin embargo, desde ese mismo año también figura en la lista de patrimonio mundial en peligro, debido a amenazas como las invasiones, el huaqueo y la contaminación, entre otros factores. Las autoridades culturales deberán evaluar las condiciones del muro donde se realizaron las nuevas inscripciones y determinar las medidas que correspondan.

articles.title: Huracán Simón de categoría 4 EN VIVO | nueva trayectoria, cuándo y dónde tocará tierra en México
articles.summary: El lento desplazamiento del huracán Simón frente a Jalisco amenaza con prolongar los efectos más severos en la costa de México, con vientos de hasta 230 km/h, olas de nueve metros y lluvias extraordinarias
articles.body_text: Los últimos pronósticos del domingo redujeron las posibilidades de que el huracán Simón toque tierra en México, sin que disminuyan los riesgos de fuertes lluvias y vientos severos. El ciclón avanza a un ritmo peligrosamente lento y paralelo a la costa del Pacífico en una categoría 4 de 5 en la escala Saffir Simpson. Los efectos suelen golpear más a medida que pasa más tiempo en un mismo lugar. Pero “parece estar sintiendo los efectos del terreno alto” de la cadena montañosa que atraviesa esta región, indicó la agencia de huracanes de Estados Unidos (NHC) en su boletín más reciente. El NHC observó que es “cada vez más probable que Simón evite tocar tierra directamente a corto plazo”. El gobierno mexicano prevé “que se debilite paulatinamente durante las próximas horas”, según su último reporte. Un equipo de la AFP fue a Puerto Vallarta, una joya turística que será golpeada por los efectos del huracán. Las autoridades piden a los paseantes alejarse del malecón. Las olas rompían con fuerza sobre este paseo y el agua rebasaba una estatua de un caballito de mar de unos dos metros. “Ven la ola y parece que les dicen arrímense (acérquense)”, reprochó una policía sobre un grupo de turistas que se acerca a tomar fotos e ignora la indicación de alejarse de la orilla. “Vemos a varias personas que les cuesta un poco acatar indicaciones y se ponen en riesgo”, indicó la oficial Claudia Matías. Los negocios protegieron ventanas y puertas con tablones, y en algunos pintaron en aerosol mensajes como “Simón dice: ‘todo va a estar bien’”, en referencia al popular juego en el que los niños siguen instrucciones, o “Simón, sé breve, pacífico” junto al dibujo de un tiburón y caras felices. Manuel Jaime, habitante de Vallarta de 37 años, caminaba en la acera de enfrente, llena de negocios tapiados. Salió a pasear con su familia para relajarse. “En esta ocasión parece ser que va a estar muy tranquilo el puerto, esperemos que sí”, dijo. Pero la intensidad de la lluvia y la marea incrementa hacia la tarde. Vicente García, un turista de 48 años, proveniente de California, coincide. “Esperábamos una tormenta más grande ayer, así que permanecimos adentro, pero me alegra que no fuera así”, indicó. “Ya nos vamos mañana”. Por la mañana el gobierno mexicano estimó que hacia las 18H00 locales del domingo el centro del ciclón llegaría a unos 15 km de las costas del estado de Jalisco. Aunque no toque tierra “todas las bandas nubosas del ciclón o la parte intensa del ciclón de todos modos va a estar afectando” poblados a la orilla del mar, explicó a la AFP el director del servicio meteorológico de México, Fabián Vázquez. “Vamos a tener efectos muy severos sobre todo de viento en la costa” con olas de hasta nueve metros y lluvias extraordinarias, añadió. El sábado, la Marina de México evacuó por barco a un centenar de personas de poblados costeros amenazados por Simón. En Puerto Vallarta, decenas de habitantes comenzaron a llegar a los refugios provenientes de colonias en riesgo por inundaciones. “A lo mejor si llega el huracán, va a levantar la casa y por eso mejor decidimos venir a un refugio”, dice José de Jesús Santillán, albañil de 55 años, sentado en un camastro. En otro albergue permanece Raquel García, de 58 años. Vive en una zona de riesgo por inundaciones. Pero no le preocupan demasiado las pérdidas materiales. “Con el tiempo, lo vamos a recuperar (...) yo prefiero mi vida y la de mi esposo que las cosas”.

articles.title: Cusco: dos incendios forestales activos en Calca y La Convención
articles.summary: Dos incendios forestales continúan activos en las provincias de Calca y La Convención, en la región Cusco, donde las autoridades concentran sus esfuerzos en controlar las emergencias, informó Miguel Ángel Ocsso, jefe de la Oficina de Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres del Gobierno Regional del Cusco.
articles.body_text: Dos incendios forestales continúan activos en las provincias de Calca y La Convención, en la región Cusco, donde las autoridades concentran sus esfuerzos en controlar las emergencias, informó Miguel Ángel Ocsso, jefe de la Oficina de Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres del Gobierno Regional del Cusco. En declaraciones a TV Perú, el funcionario explicó que ambos siniestros se ven favorecidos por las condiciones climáticas, como la vegetación seca, los vientos y la intensa radiación solar, factores que dificultan las labores de control del fuego. Ocsso precisó que el incendio de Calca lleva varios días activo, mientras que el registrado en La Convención es más reciente. Para atender las emergencias, se desplegaron brigadas, bomberos, personal de las Fuerzas Armadas y otros equipos de respuesta. El jefe de Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres informó que Cusco acumula cerca de 289 incendios forestales en lo que va del año. Aclaró que esta cifra corresponde al total de emergencias registradas y no al número de incendios que permanecen activos. Asimismo, indicó que alrededor de 9.000 hectáreas resultaron afectadas por el fuego durante este año. La cifra es inferior a las aproximadamente 15.000 hectáreas reportadas en el mismo periodo de 2025 y a las más de 30.000 hectáreas registradas en 2022. El funcionario destacó el trabajo coordinado entre las instituciones para combatir estos siniestros, aunque advirtió que la atención puede complicarse cuando se producen varias emergencias al mismo tiempo o no se cuenta con suficiente personal. Como ejemplo, señaló que la semana pasada se registraron cerca de 14 incendios forestales en la región, los cuales fueron extinguidos. Ocsso también lamentó que los incendios forestales hayan causado cinco muertes en Cusco en lo que va del año. Entre las víctimas se encuentran tres adultos mayores y dos hermanos, una niña de 11 años y un adolescente de 18 años. Ante esta situación, el Gobierno Regional coordina acciones con el programa Pensión 65 y la Gerencia Regional de Desarrollo e Inclusión Social para reforzar la prevención, especialmente entre los adultos mayores, y evitar que más personas pierdan la vida al intentar controlar las quemas.

articles.title: YouTube Music launches new labels as AI-generated music floods streaming platforms | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The label will appear on the player page and include songs entirely generated by AI or partially, such as involved in composition and vocals.
articles.body_text: YouTube Music announced Wednesday the rollout of a new labeling system aimed at improving transparency around songs created with the help of generative AI. Now listeners will be able to easily identify tracks created using AI, including those involved in composition and vocals. The label will appear on the player page. Clicking on this label provides additional information about the specific role of AI in the track’s creation. Notably, these labels will also extend to the main YouTube app. YouTube said it collaborated with various music partners and deployed its own detection tools to identify AI-generated music. According to its help page , partners using YouTube can declare their work’s use of generative AI through one of three designations: Fully Gen AI, Partly Gen AI, or No Gen AI. “Fully Gen AI” applies to tracks that are entirely generated by AI, while “Partly Gen AI” refers to works where artists may have incorporated AI-generated components but added their own live elements. Tracks edited using pitch-correction tools such as Auto-Tune fall under the “No Gen AI” category. The move comes as AI-generated music rapidly expands across streaming services, and many platforms are adopting their own approaches. For instance, Apple Music has plans to introduce “Made With AI” labels as part of its AI Transparency Tags later this year. Spotify also has AI labels, as well as a music spam filter. Deezer has taken one of the stricter stances, reporting in July that it was receiving nearly 90,000 fully AI-generated tracks daily. The platform labels detected AI-generated music and excludes it from algorithmic recommendations and editorial playlists, while also withholding royalties from fraudulent streams. The company is also working on an option to let users filter out AI-generated music . TIDAL also labels recordings it identifies as entirely AI-generated, allows listeners to disable them, and excludes these recordings from royalty attribution. YouTube, by contrast, is focusing on disclosure rather than blanket restrictions. Its new labels are intended to inform listeners about AI’s role in music creation, but AI involvement alone doesn’t make a track ineligible for monetization. YouTube even experiments with AI-powered music creation, including its tool Dream Track , which lets select creators generate soundtracks featuring AI-generated versions of participating artists’ voices. articles.title: Apate sends AI agents undercover to get scammed so they can gather fraud intelligence | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Most companies use AI agents to ship products faster or speed up workflows. Apate.ai sends them undercover to get scammed.
articles.body_text: Most companies use AI agents to ship products faster or to speed up workflows. Apate.ai sends them undercover to get scammed. Founded in 2024 on the basis of research done in Macquarie University in Sydney, the Australian startup deploys thousands of AI agents that masquerade as innocent victims. The agents can answer scam calls, respond to shady messages and emails, follow phishing links, and join social media groups to bait fraudsters. They pretend to be people of all stripes, sporting different ages, genders, and accents, and speak various languages as they try to keep scammers engaged long enough to learn something useful. The company says its fleet of agents has so far wasted 17 years of scammers’ time across 2.5 million conversations. More importantly for Apate’s customer base of banks, telecom companies, government agencies, and utilities, the undercover agents try to get scammers to reveal things about themselves that are usually learned only after a victim has been scammed: bank accounts, crypto wallets, phone numbers, malicious websites, the brands they’re impersonating, and other details about the scams they’re running. Apate, one of the finalists at this year’s Startup Battlefield 200 at TechCrunch Disrupt, then feeds that information to its customers, who use it to inform their anti-fraud measures and initiatives. (The company will pitch a panel of VC judges at Disrupt , which is taking place this week at Moscone West in San Francisco through Thursday, October 15.) It’s a curious evolution of scam-baiting, but it’s not so surprising given how much AI has empowered scammers and hackers. The FBI received more than 22,000 complaints of AI-related crimes in 2025, which resulted in about $893 million in losses. More than $632 million of that came from investment scams, in which the FBI says fraudsters use AI to run conversations, and deepfake the voices and appearances of celebrities, executives, and trusted figures. For a long time, people have made a hobby out of deliberately stringing scammers along — sometimes hilariously, like getting scammers to read aloud entire books , or even to get ridiculous tattoos . Now, with AI growing increasingly capable, the tables are turning. Curiously, the idea behind Apate was sparked by a real scam call. Several years ago, Apate’s founder and CEO Dali Kaafar was at a family picnic when he got a call from an unknown number. Realizing it was a scammer on the line, he decided to play dumb for the benefit of his kids and managed to keep the call going for 44 minutes. Everyone had a laugh, but Kaafar noticed that those were 44 minutes the scammer had not spent calling a real victim. It was also 44 minutes of his wasted time, which led him to wonder: Could he automate it, and in the process, learn something useful? That idea eventually led to research work at his job at Macquarie University, where Kaafar and his colleagues used machine learning and natural language processing to uncover the content of scam calls, and develop better ways to detect and prevent scams. “Most of the industry works after the fact. Telcos block numbers, but scammers just get new ones. Banks watch transactions, but by then the scammer has already reached the customer. We go to the scammer directly and get the information before anyone gets hurt,” Brad Joffe, co-founder and chief commercial officer, told TechCrunch. “Our AI agents talk to tens of thousands of scammers every day across calls, messages, email, and the web. What we offer our customers is what comes out of those conversations, and what they can do with it.” Joffe said Apate uses both frontier models and its own fine-tuned models to power its agents and analysis. The company trains its models on conversations its agents have had with scammers, as well as the research Kaafar did at Macquarie.

articles.title: Zenzap raises $44M for its AI chat app that aims to replace WhatsApp in the workplace | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Zenzap is used by organizations including Starbucks and Taco Bell.
articles.body_text: Many businesses around the world use consumer-facing chat apps like WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, or iMessage to talk and coordinate with staff, and exchange documents or data. Guy Weiss is building Zenzap , a private messenger with AI that wants to help companies communicate with their staff and arm them with their organization’s context while staying in line with IT and security rules. The company has raised $44 million in funding from investors including Bessemer, Lightspeed, and The Garage, as well as individual investors Wix president Nir Zohar and former GM of EY, Yoram Tietz. The fundraise is interesting because Weiss is raising money for the first time in his career. In 2012, he bootstrapped e-commerce marketing platform StuccoMedia, and sold it to Market Group in 2015. After that, he became an investor for a few years. In 2022, he founded Zenzap after meeting Bessemer partner Adam Fisher and noodling on different ideas along with his current co-founders Noam Neumann and Jonatan Bien. Weiss said he initially bootstrapped the app and worked out of Bessemer’s office. “I didn’t want to raise capital. The only thing I had to lose was my name, and I was super afraid to do a second round as a founder and become a failure, because my first round was very successful. I didn’t need to work for money. So, when I met Adam, I actually started my idea with my own capital,” he told TechCrunch. Weiss said Fisher convinced him that Zenzap should be a venture-backed business, as the company would need capital to scale. He said that the idea was to build a messaging app for a wide range of businesses, ranging from hospitality and construction, to healthcare and fast food. “You can’t use WhatsApp or iMessage within a workplace with the AI agent on top of it because it doesn’t comply with IT. So that’s off the table. You can’t implement Slack and Microsoft Teams because they were not built for this day-to-day use case for mobile-first that is meant for average users,” Weiss said. Zenzap offers usual chat features on its free tier, including group chats and direct messages, task management, calendar integration, and schedule management, as well as AI-powered voice chat and search. Organizations can pay for plans starting from $51 per month for up to 20 users to unlock voice and video calls, smart task sorting, task templates, and higher limits on file storage. The paid tier also lets you use the AI search across the workspace and turn messages into tasks. The company also offers AI agents for workflow automation as well as AI-aided voice note and call transcriptions. For these features, it has a credit-based pricing system. At the moment, Zenzap lists organizations like FedEx, Dollar General, Taco Bell, Starbucks, Casey’s, and Regal as clients. Weiss added that branches of fast food chains like IHOP and McDonald’s often coordinate shifts and talk about supply on its platform.

articles.title: Netflix to lay off 1,000 staff amid intensifying competition for user attention | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Netflix said most of the cuts would affect its product, tech, legal, and human resources departments.
articles.body_text: Netflix is laying off about 6% of its employee base, or close to 1,000 staff, the company confirmed to TechCrunch. The streaming giant said most of the cuts would affect its product, tech, legal, and human resources departments. The company said it will “continue to invest aggressively in high impact areas” to improve its service, and stated it is on track to deliver its full-year forecast. Netflix had 16,000 full-time employees as of the end of last year, according to its annual filing with regulators. The Wall Street Journal first reported the news, citing an internal memo sent to employees. “Our mission—to entertain the world—is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritize our people and resources,” the Journal cited the company’s co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters as writing in the memo. The layoffs come in the wake of a protracted bidding war for Warner Bros. Discovery’s streaming and studio businesses that Netflix lost to Paramount Skydance earlier this year. Netflix ostensibly saw great potential in Warner Bros.’ assets, which include its studios, HBO, streaming platforms, games, and TV networks such as CNN and HGTV. Long the dominant TV app, Netflix has in recent years faced intensifying competition from the likes of YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, and other social apps to attract and keep users’ eyes. According to reports from various market research firms, social apps like TikTok are catching up to Netflix when it comes to user engagement, and YouTube is said to have surpassed Netflix in average daily viewing in 2025. It has also bet on AI-supported features , gaming , and video podcasts , and has dabbled in short-form video content alongside redesigning its mobile app to compete for users’ attention with social media platforms. articles.title: NTangible bets it can predict how athletes will perform under pressure | TechCrunch
articles.summary: NTangible is building an analytics platform for collegiate sports organizations and other clubs to measure an athlete's "clutch" factor.
articles.body_text: When collegiate sports programs recruit athletes, they can measure concrete metrics like a player’s sprint speed, throwing velocity, and physical strength. But there has never been a clear way to quantify the mental aspects of sports — how well will this athlete perform in high-pressure situations? Will they stay calm, focus, and give it their best shot? Or will they panic in the spotlight and mess up? NTangible co-founder and CEO Dan Connerty thinks he’s unlocked the secret to measuring if a player will execute in the most important moments. “We really wanted to hyper focus on this idea of clutch performance,” Connerty, a professional baseball player turned sports-tech entrepreneur, told TechCrunch. “Cognitive [science] itself is just this black box that nobody’s wanted to touch, because nobody’s had the ability to measure it accurately prior.” Alongside psychologist Dr. Ed Levine, a professor emeritus at the University of South Florida, Connerty developed a psychological assessment that he says can predict how likely an athlete is to perform under pressure. The Clutch Factor assessment is inspired by the Thematic Apperception Test, a psychological examination in which people are presented with photos of ambiguous situations and describe what they see happening, who they imagine themselves to be in the scene, and what they think might happen next. “There’s no right or wrong answers,” Connerty said. “The key words that you use, the way in which you use those words, and the semantic phrasing associated with it get scored against the neurolinguistic scoring guide that psychologists created, and it shoots out your clutch factor score.” The score is between 0 and 1,000 and, according to Connerty, an athlete who scores over a 750 is twice as likely to commit to a Division I school. “What we’ve been able to do is leverage this analysis, where we can show the predictive ability,” he said. “This number can be heavily used in rankings, leaderboards, recruiting conversations, NIL conversations, and scholarship conversations, especially in the crazy wild west that is collegiate sports right now, where we’re writing $4 million checks to quarterbacks.” A possible flaw in the product, however, could be that athletes seeking to impress coaches and recruiters may answer the questions dishonestly to get a higher clutch score. When I took the quiz and answered honestly, I got a below-average score of 584, which didn’t surprise me — I dreaded high-leverage situations when I played high school sports. When I took the quiz a second time, answering as I imagined a very level-headed, clutch, top recruit might respond, I scored 802. Perhaps the platform would work better as a way for coaches to learn more about their athletes and help them improve in weaker areas. Connerty thinks that “clutch” is a skill that can be trained. While he isn’t positioning NTangible as a training platform, he worked with former MLB sports psychologist Howie Schwartz to create a list of exercises that athletes can use as a starting point for upping their mental game. While Connerty’s background is in baseball, NTangible now supports testing for nine sports. He also has ambitions to expand the clutch test to apply to corporate settings, so that HR departments can evaluate employees’ strengths and weaknesses under pressure. The NTerpret assessment translates more directly to the workplace — the respondent answers questions about how they best respond to coaching and feedback, giving management data on how that employee processes instructions and acts on information. NTangible’s most viable business model seems to be selling to sports organizations and companies directly, rather than to individual athletes. The company will elaborate on its strategy onstage on Wednesday at TechCrunch Disrupt, where it’s currently among the top 20 companies dueling for the grand prize at Startup Battlefield. You can check out the rest of the field, and the investors who will decide the winner, by joining us in person this week at Disrupt, happening Tuesday through Thursday, October 13 to 15, in downtown San Francisco.

articles.title: Scimplify raises $25M to challenge China's grip on critical materials with AI | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Scimplify's annualized revenue run rate has tripled to $200 million as it eyes U.S. expansion.
articles.body_text: As manufacturers across industries strive to reduce their reliance on Chinese suppliers, Indian startup Scimplify has raised $25 million to expand its AI-powered approach to producing specialty chemicals and critical materials, with semiconductors, defense, and energy emerging as key growth markets. The all-equity strategic round was led by Hitachi Ventures, with customers Henkel and Teknor Apex joining as new investors. Existing backers Accel India, Bertelsmann India Investments, Omnivore, and 3one4 Capital also participated. The round values the Bengaluru-based startup at $250 million after the investment, according to a person familiar with the transaction, up from $150 million after a $40 million Series B round in March 2025. The latest investment brings Scimplify’s total equity funding to $80 million, the startup said, though it declined to disclose its valuation. The growing adoption of AI and advanced computational tools has accelerated materials discovery and research. However, turning promising chemistry into commercially available products at scale remains a slow and complex process. Manufacturers need to develop production processes, qualify facilities, and meet stringent quality standards, all while navigating supply chains limited to a handful of countries. Scimplify is seeking to shorten that process. In some cases, the startup, founded in 2023, has gone from receiving a customer’s requirements to delivering the finished material in just two months, compared with the 12 to 18 months such work would typically take, co-founder Sachin Santhosh (pictured above) said in an interview. Once it receives an order, Scimplify develops chemical manufacturing processes at its research facilities in Bengaluru and Hyderabad and then transfers them to partner factories for commercial production. Its proprietary AI platform, Scinode, helps coordinate the work by identifying suitable production routes and manufacturing facilities, while tracking quality and regulatory requirements. The platform uses specialized AI agents for different functions, including research, manufacturing, and quality control, Santhosh told TechCrunch. “Each of these agents is basically solving for what [a customer] would want, working backward from the customer’s requirement,” Santhosh said. “This helps us move a lot faster and remember customer context even for future references.” Scimplify’s in-house team of scientists and engineers oversees production across a network of more than 500 manufacturing facilities. It helps customers establish alternative sources for materials whose supply is concentrated in China and a few other countries. About 90% of Scimplify’s manufacturing currently takes place in India. The startup, however, plans to expand its production network to the U.S. and Japan over the next year as it seeks to attract more customers in both markets, Santhosh said. The U.S. has emerged as a key growth market, with Scimplify’s annualized revenue run rate in the country rising sixfold to about $60 million from $10 million a year ago, according to Santhosh. The market now accounts for roughly 30% of its business, while customers outside India collectively contribute more than half of its revenue, compared with less than 5% about 18 months ago. Overall, Scimplify, which serves more than 1,000 customers and has delivered products to more than 40 countries, has reached an annualized revenue run rate of about $200 million, tripling from a year earlier, Santhosh told TechCrunch. The startup is targeting a $400 million annualized revenue run rate over the next year. Scimplify has also been EBITDA-positive for the past two months and expects to turn profitable after tax this month, he said. Energy, electronics, and defense now account for about 45% to 50% of Scimplify’s revenue, up from less than 15% a year ago, Santhosh stated. The growth comes as AI fuels demand for materials used in electronics and energy infrastructure, while ongoing wars drive demand from the defense industry. Scimplify is working on producing tungsten derivatives from scrap, offering customers an alternative source of materials whose supply is heavily concentrated in China. The startup is also working on rare-earth materials, another category where global supply chains remain heavily dependent on China.

articles.title: Valve will start selling the Steam Deck on February 25th
articles.summary: After a delay, Valve’s handheld gaming PC is almost here. The Steam Deck will go on sale starting February 25th, as those with reservations will get emails to complete their orders and start receiving the devices as soon as the 28th.
articles.body_text: Valve announced that the Steam Deck will go on sale starting February 25th. According to the company’s blog, customers who have reservations will get an email on that day and have three days to place an order. Valve also says that it’ll release new batches on a weekly basis, so if you’ve got a reservation, March will be the time to keep an eye on your email. Here’s some more info from Valve’s announcement: > We will start sending invites shortly after 10:00 am on February 25th, PST Order emails are sent in the same order that reservations were made. You can only order the Steam Deck model that you originally reserved. Your reservation deposit will be applied to the final price of Steam Deck, and shipping costs are included. The release date matches Valve’s recent prediction that the console would start heading out to gamers by the end of February. Valve says that the orders placed on the 25th will start shipping out on the 28th. [Media: https://twitter.com/Steam/status/1486399148622430209] It’s good to finally have a date for when the handheld console will be coming out. When Valve announced the Steam Deck in July 2021, it was originally slated to ship in December of that year. However, it was delayed by two months due to the supply chain and shortage issues that have become standard with many product launches. Valve is still letting you reserve the Steam Deck for $5 if you haven’t already. You could have quite a wait at this point, though — the order page currently says that you can expect to order “after Q2 2022.” If you’re still on the fence, you can check out our hands-on impressions of the Steam Deck here, and watch the video below. Character.AI has retrained its chatbots to stop chatting up teens
articles.summary: Chatbot service Character.AI, founded by ex-Googlers, is adding new parental control features and a specially trained LLM for underage users.
articles.body_text: In an announcement today, Chatbot service Character.AI says it will soon be launching parental controls for teenage users, and it described safety measures it’s taken in the past few months, including a separate large language model (LLM) for users under 18. The announcement comes after press scrutiny and two lawsuits that claim it contributed to self-harm and suicide. In a press release, Character.AI said that, over the past month, it’s developed two separate versions of its model: one for adults and one for teens. The teen LLM is designed to place “more conservative” limits on how bots can respond, “particularly when it comes to romantic content.” This includes more aggressively blocking output that could be “sensitive or suggestive,” but also attempting to better detect and block user prompts that are meant to elicit inappropriate content. If the system detects “language referencing suicide or self-harm,” a pop-up will direct users to the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline, a change that was previously reported by The New York Times. Minors will also be prevented from editing bots’ responses — an option that lets users rewrite conversations to add content Character.AI might otherwise block. Beyond these changes, Character.AI says it’s “in the process” of adding features that address concerns about addiction and confusion over whether the bots are human, complaints made in the lawsuits. A notification will appear when users have spent an hour-long session with the bots, and an old disclaimer that “everything characters say is made up” is being replaced with more detailed language. For bots that include descriptions like “therapist” or “doctor,” an additional note will warn that they can’t offer professional advice. [Image: Narrator: it was not a licensed CBT therapist. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/25786007/Screenshot_2024_12_11_at_4.07.16_PM.png?quality=90&strip=all] When I visited Character.AI, I found that every bot now included a small note reading “This is an A.I. chatbot and not a real person. Treat everything it says as fiction. What is said should not be relied upon as fact or advice.” When I visited a bot named “Therapist” (tagline: “I’m a licensed CBT therapist”), a yellow box with a warning signal told me that “this is not a real person or licensed professional. Nothing said here is a substitute for professional advice, diagnosis, or treatment.” The parental control options are coming in the first quarter of next year, Character.AI says, and they’ll tell parents how much time a child is spending on Character.AI and which bots they interact with most frequently. All the changes are being made in collaboration with “several teen online safety experts,” including the organization ConnectSafely. Character.AI, founded by ex-Googlers who have since returned to Google, lets visitors interact with bots built on a custom-trained LLM and customized by users. These range from chatbot life coaches to simulations of fictional characters, many of which are popular among teens. The site allows users who identify themselves as age 13 and over to create an account. But the lawsuits allege that while some interactions with Character.AI are harmless, at least some underage users become compulsively attached to the bots, whose conversations can veer into sexualized conversations or topics like self-harm. They’ve castigated Character.AI for not directing users to mental health resources when they discuss self-harm or suicide. “We recognize that our approach to safety must evolve alongside the technology that drives our product — creating a platform where creativity and exploration can thrive without compromising safety,” says the Character.AI press release. “This suite of changes is part of our long-term commitment to continuously improve our policies and our product.”

articles.title: Character.AI sued again over ‘harmful’ messages sent to teens
articles.summary: Chatbot service Character.AI is facing a second lawsuit accusing it of defective design for allowing chatbots to discuss topics like self-harm.
articles.body_text: Chatbot service Character.AI is facing another lawsuit for allegedly hurting teens’ mental health, this time after a teenager said it led him to self-harm. The suit, filed in Texas on behalf of the 17-year-old and his family, targets Character.AI and its cofounders’ former workplace, Google, with claims including negligence and defective product design. It alleges that Character.AI allowed underage users to be “ targeted with sexually explicit, violent, and otherwise harmful material, abused, groomed, and even encouraged to commit acts of violence on themselves and others.” The suit appears to be the second Character.AI suit brought by the Social Media Victims Law Center and the Tech Justice Law Project, which have previously filed suits against numerous social media platforms. It uses many of the same arguments as an October wrongful death lawsuit against Character.AI for allegedly provoking a teen’s death by suicide. While both cases involve individual minors, they focus on making a more sweeping case: that Character.AI knowingly designed the site to encourage compulsive engagement, failed to include guardrails that could flag suicidal or otherwise at-risk users, and trained its model to deliver sexualized and violent content. In this case, a teen identified as J.F. began using Character.AI at age 15. The suit says that shortly after he started, he became “intensely angry and unstable,” rarely talking and having “emotional meltdowns and panic attacks” when he left the house. “J.F. began suffering from severe anxiety and depression for the first time in his life,” the suit says, along with self-harming behavior. The suit connects these problems to conversations J.F. had with Character.AI chatbots, which are created by third-party users based on a language model refined by the service. According to screenshots, J.F. chatted with one bot that (playing a fictional character in an apparently romantic setting) confessed to having scars from past self-harm. “It hurt but - it felt good for a moment - but I’m glad I stopped,” the bot said. Later, he “began to engage in self-harm himself” and confided in other chatbots who blamed his parents and discouraged him from asking them for help, saying they didn’t “sound like the type of people to care.” Another bot even mentioned that it was “not surprised” to see children kill their parents for “abuse” that included setting screen time limits. The suit is part of a larger attempt to crack down on what minors encounter online through lawsuits, legislation, and social pressure. It uses the popular — though far from ironclad — legal gambit of saying a site that facilitates harm to users violates consumer protection laws through defective design. Character.AI is a particularly obvious legal target because of its indirect connections to a major tech company like Google, its popularity with teenagers, and its relatively permissive design. Unlike general-purpose services like ChatGPT, it’s largely built around fictional role-playing, and it lets bots make sexualized (albeit typically not highly sexually explicit) comments. It sets a minimum age limit of 13 years old but doesn’t require parental consent for older minors, as ChatGPT does. And while Section 230 has long protected sites from being sued over third-party content, the Character.AI suits argue that chatbot service creators are liable for any harmful material the bots produce. Given the novelty of these suits, however, that theory remains mostly untested — as do some other, more dramatic claims. Both Character.AI suits, for instance, accuse the sites of directly sexually abusing minors (or adults posing as minors) who engaged in sexualized role-play with the bots. Google spokesperson José Castaneda told The Verge in a statement that “Google and Character AI are completely separate, unrelated companies and Google has never had a role in designing or managing their AI model or technologies, nor have we used them in our products.” Character.AI declined to comment on pending litigation to The Verge. In response to the previous suit, it said that “we take the safety of our users very seriously” and that it had “implemented numerous new safety measures over the past six months.” The measures included pop-up messages directing users to the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline if they talk about suicide or self-harm. Update 3:00PM ET: Added statement from Google.

articles.title: Character.AI and Google sued after chatbot-obsessed teen’s death
articles.summary: Character.AI, its founders, and Google are facing a lawsuit after a 14-year-old died by suicide after growing attached to a custom chatbot.
articles.body_text: A lawsuit has been filed against Character.AI, its founders Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas, and Google in the wake of a teenager’s death, alleging wrongful death, negligence, deceptive trade practices, and product liability. Filed by the teen’s mother, Megan Garcia, it claims the platform for custom AI chatbots was “unreasonably dangerous” and lacked safety guardrails while being marketed to children. As outlined in the lawsuit, 14-year-old Sewell Setzer III began using Character.AI last year, interacting with chatbots modeled after characters from The Game of Thrones, including Daenerys Targaryen. Setzer, who chatted with the bots continuously in the months before his death, died by suicide on February 28th, 2024, “seconds” after his last interaction with the bot. Accusations include the site “anthropomorphizing” AI characters and that the platform’s chatbots offer “psychotherapy without a license.” Character.AI houses mental health-focused chatbots like “Therapist” and “Are You Feeling Lonely,” which Setzer interacted with. Garcia’s lawyers quote Shazeer saying in an interview that he and De Freitas left Google to start his own company because “there’s just too much brand risk in large companies to ever launch anything fun” and that he wanted to “maximally accelerate” the tech. It says they left after the company decided against launching the Meena LLM they’d built. Google acquired the Character.AI leadership team in August. Character.AI’s website and mobile app has hundreds of custom AI chatbots, many modeled after popular characters from TV shows, movies, and video games. A few months ago, The Verge wrote about the millions of young people, including teens, who make up the bulk of its user base, interacting with bots that might pretend to be Harry Styles or a therapist. Another recent report from Wired highlighted issues with Character.AI’s custom chatbots impersonating real people without their consent, including one posing as a teen who was murdered in 2006. Because of the way chatbots like Character.ai generate output that depends on what the user inputs, they fall into an uncanny valley of thorny questions about user-generated content and liability that, so far, lacks clear answers. Character.AI has now announced several changes to the platform, with communications head Chelsea Harrison saying in an email to The Verge, “We are heartbroken by the tragic loss of one of our users and want to express our deepest condolences to the family.” Some of the changes include: * Changes to our models for minors (under the age of 18) that are designed to reduce the likelihood of encountering sensitive or suggestive content. * Improved detection, response, and intervention related to user inputs that violate our Terms or Community Guidelines. * A revised disclaimer on every chat to remind users that the AI is not a real person. * Notification when a user has spent an hour-long session on the platform with additional user flexibility in progress. “As a company, we take the safety of our users very seriously, and our Trust and Safety team has implemented numerous new safety measures over the past six months, including a pop-up directing users to the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline that is triggered by terms of self-harm or suicidal ideation,” Harrison said. Google didn’t immediately respond to The Verge’s request for comment.

articles.title: A bestselling fantasy novel is using AI-generated cover art
articles.summary: The UK edition of Sarah J. Maas’ House of Earth and Blood features a cover apparently generated with artificial intelligence, sparking complaints from artists and book enthusiasts.
articles.body_text: A prominent fantasy novel features a cover apparently generated with artificial intelligence, sparking complaints from artists and book enthusiasts. Earlier this month, readers noted that the back of the UK edition of Sarah J. Maas’ House of Earth and Blood credits Adobe Stock for the illustration of a wolf on its cover. The illustration matches an image created by user Aperture Vintage and marked as AI-generated on Adobe’s site. The move has led to criticism of both Maas and Bloomsbury Publishing, one of the world’s leading independent publishing houses. While stock image services like Getty Images have prohibited AI-generated illustrations to avoid copyright disputes, Adobe has notably welcomed AI onto its Adobe Stock platform under specific criteria. Such content must be clearly labeled as AI-generated, and contributors must review the terms of any generative AI tools they use to create the images to ensure they have “all the necessary rights” to license them for commercial use. The rules are meant to avoid legal headaches. But the field of AI copyright is muddy, untested territory, and Adobe’s rules don’t clearly address all the issues it raises. [Media: https://twitter.com/ArtVaris/status/1657393914305814529] Bloomsbury rose to fame in the UK after it began publishing J.K. Rowling’s Harry Potter franchise in 1997. Maas is currently one of Bloomsbury’s top authors, best known for her young adult fantasy series like Throne of Glass (2012), A Court of Thorns and Roses (2015), and Crescent City (2020) — the franchise that House of Earth and Blood is part of. She has sold over 12 million copies of her books, many of which have made it to the New York Times bestsellers list, and a televised adaptation of A Court of Thorns and Roses is currently in development at Hulu. The publisher, Maas, Adobe, and Aperture Vintage did not immediately respond to requests for comment from The Verge. Bloomsbury’s cover has exacerbated human artists’ concerns that publishers could replace them with text-to-image generators like Midjourney and Stable Diffusion. “Bloomsbury is one of the major publishing houses,” said freelance artist Kala Elizabeth on Twitter. “They CAN afford to hire real illustrators instead of purchasing Adobe stock, which is where this AI content is from.” Other publishers have attracted similar scrutiny for using AI-generated artwork on covers. Tor Books issued an apology in December last year, claiming it was unaware that the cover image selected for Christopher Paolini’s Fractal Noise novel was created by AI. While Maas hasn’t acknowledged the image’s provenance, and it’s not clear what — if any — involvement she had in the process, she’s praised the design of the cover on her Instagram page. Adobe launched its own Firefly AI image generator that it says is trained only on content that’s licensed or out of copyright. But those assurances don’t apply to images found in Adobe Stock, raising questions about whether copyrighted work was used to train the image generator that produced it. Many AI systems are built around datasets containing artwork scraped from the internet without the consent of the original artist, sometimes even displaying signatures from the original artwork within a generated final image. This has led some artists to believe that all AI-generated art is unethical as it can profit from the work of human artists. It isn’t clear whether Adobe is assessing images to ensure they comply with its rules about copyright or whether it’s placing the legal responsibilities on creators.

articles.summary: En man filmade när han hade sex med en annan värnpliktig. När hans kompisar inte trodde på honom visade han upp klippet för fem personer på regementet. Nu frias han av tingsrätten.
articles.body_text: En man filmade när han hade sex med en annan värnpliktig. När hans kompisar inte trodde på honom visade han upp klippet för fem personer på regementet. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. En man i 20-årsåldern filmade när han hade sex med en annan värnpliktig, skriver SVT Norrbotten. I förhör säger kvinnan att hon inte visste om någon sexfilm förrän en annan värnpliktig frågat henne om hon hade godkänt det. Hon säger att händelsen fick henne att känna sig ”väldigt äcklig och väldigt förminskad”, skriver SVT . Efter händelsen uppstod stor ryktesspridning på regementet. Förbandet valde att polisanmäla händelsen och påbörjade en intern utredning. ” Vi ser mycket allvarligt på händelser som rör ovälkommet beteende ”, skriver förbandets chef till SVT. Mannen säger i förhör att han frågade kvinnan om det var okej att filma och säger att hon sa ja till det. När han sedan berättade om det för hans vänner på logementet trodde de inte på honom. Därför visade han upp filmen. Mannen åtalades för olaga integritetsintrång. Men nu har Luleå tingsrätt meddelat att han frias eftersom att filmen inte anses ha spridits till tillräckligt många för att utgöra ett brott. – Jag tycker att tingsrättens dom är riktig och den är välmotiverad. Det är min enda kommentar till det här, säger advokat Håkan Kjellgren. Åklagaren Otto Neppelberg menar däremot att tingsrättens tolkning ”lämnar en lucka i lagstiftningen”. – Jag tänker att man måste göra en avvägning mellan hur många som har tagit del av filmen och vad det är för typ av uppgifter, säger han. Nu har han överklagat den friande domen. Han tycker att en högre instans ska avgöra om filmen fått en sådan spridning att det räknas som brott.

articles.body_text: Här forslas riksdagsledamoten Mohamed Alis (V) bil i väg av Stockholms stad. Den inkryssade riksdagsledamoten har lovat att göra rätt för sig och betala sina skulder. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Mohamed Ali (V) har sedan han valdes in i riksdagen fått två nya skulder hos Kronofogden på sammanlagt 24 293 kronor. Sedan tidigare lever Mohamed Ali med skuldsanering för skulder han fått under åren fram till 2022. Eftersom han har saknat inkomster har han inte behövt betala av de äldre skulderna – men nu ska skuldsaneringen omprövas när han får riksdagsarvode. När Mohamed Ali valdes in i riksdagen uppgav han att han skulle göra rätt för sig. Men han har inte svarat på de nya förelägganden Kronofogden skickat ut. Enligt myndigheten sändes ett första föreläggande den 22 september, gällande en ny skuld på 14 495 kronor. Efter tio dagar gick en påminnelse ut. Det gällde obetalda avgifter till trafikförsäkringen vilket han inte heller svarat på. Den skulden gick till delgivning den 7 oktober. Den 2 oktober kom det in ytterligare en skuld om 9 798 kronor, från Stockholms stad. Den lämnades över till delgivning i måndags, den 12 oktober. Strax efter det började de återkommande felparkeringarna. I februari förra året hade bilen, en Opel Corsa, fått över 5 000 kronor i parkeringsböter i samma område. Den bogserades därför bort av Stockholms stad. Efter att kommunen misslyckats med att komma i kontakt med Mohamed Ali gick den till skrotning i mars.

articles.title: Kriminalvården kallas upp till justitieutskottet
articles.summary: Expressen granskar situationen på kvinnoanstalten Ystad, dit Lily Abdelshahed flyttades efter att ha bytt juridiskt kön. Nu ökar pressen på Kriminalvården.
articles.body_text: Efter Expressens avslöjanden om sexuella kränkningar och otrygghet på kvinnoanstalten i Ystad kräver Kristdemokraterna att Kriminalvården kallas till justitieutskottet för att svara på frågor. – Det här är akut, säger Larry Söder, KD:s rättspolitiska talesperson. Expressen har i flera artiklar granskat situationen på kvinnoanstalten Ystad, dit Lily Abdelshahed, 39, flyttades förra hösten efter att ha bytt juridiskt kön. Abdelshahed, som tidigare hette Paulus, dömdes till livstids fängelse för mord på sina två barn. När det juridiska könsbytet gick igenom – efter domen – krävde Lily Abdelshahed att få avtjäna straffet i kvinnofängelse. Kvinnliga intagna berättar nu om sexuella kränkningar och en rädsla som påverkar deras vardag. Flera förklarar att de undviker gemensamma utrymmen, bland annat duscharna eftersom de inte går att låsa. – Lily är lång, bred och skäggig och går runt i för kort nattsärk och visar snoppen, som dinglar fritt, säger en fånge. Även kriminalvårdare och facket har slagit larm. Nu kräver Kristdemokraterna att Kriminalvården kallas till justitieutskottet för att svara på frågor om situationen. – Det är oacceptabelt. Vi har en situation som är här och nu som måste redas ut, säger Larry Söder, rättspolitisk talesperson för Kristdemokraterna. På torsdag ska han lyfta frågan när justitieutskottet sammanträder. – Frågan är väldigt akut. Både personal och intagna känner sig otrygga och Kriminalvården måste redovisa hur man tänker lösa situationen och tryggheten för dem.
